finding.evidence: order 1002 (name, e-mail, address, card ending) returned without any session
finding.description: Any order is readable by changing the number.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: idor (Any order is readable by changing the number. Evidence: order 1002 (name, e-mail, address, card ending) returned without any session). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Enforce server-side authorization on every order access: require an authenticated session and implement access control checks for each object that users try to access, verifying the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object such as database keys, file names, or record IDs before returning data.

sources.contribution: To mitigate IDOR, implement access control checks for each object that users try to access.

IDOR occurs when an application exposes internal object references such as database keys, file names, or record IDs and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.

verification.claim: IDOR occurs when an application exposes internal object references such as database keys, file names, or record IDs and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.
verification.detail: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) is an access control vulnerability that occurs when an application exposes internal object references — such as database keys, file names, or record IDs — and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.

fix.summary: Enforce ownership check on /order: only the customer cookie matching the order email (or admin) can view it, otherwise 403.
fix.risk: Requests with wrong or missing customer cookie now get 403; admin session still allowed.
